sense: the making or growing of goods

evidence: Pall. Nov. 5: oleī, oil-making (Lewis & Short; late)
terms.comment: Several times in Cicero, elsewhere rare (Lewis & Short); with the genitive of what is made.

evidence: M-O s.v. production of goods, industrial production (Egger)
terms.comment: Classically effectiō belongs to Cicero’s philosophical prose (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Mihi quidem ita jūcunda hujus librī cōnfectiō fuit, ut … effēcerit mollem etiam et jūcundam senectūtem.
phrases.english: The making of this book has been such a pleasure to me that it has even made old age gentle and pleasant.

phrases.latin: ut ūberī vīneārum prōventū bene dōlia picārentur
phrases.english: that, since the vines had yielded richly, the wine jars should be well pitched

sources: Lewis & Short: confectio · Lewis & Short: proventus · Lewis & Short: effectio
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. production of goods, industrial production.
